2027-07-03.title: Dukhrana of Saint Thomas the Apostle
2027-07-03.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: God plants a garden in Eden, in the east
Keep hold of instruction, for she is your life
The household of God, built on the foundation of the apostles
It is to peace that God has called you
What God has joined together, let no one separate
2027-07-03.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), which began at Pentecost: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, carried the Gospel to the nations. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari. This is the last weekend of the season: the Season of Kaitha begins on Sunday 4 July. Today is the Dukhrana of Saint Thomas the Apostle, an important feast and a day of obligation in the Syro-Malabar calendar, and also the Seventh Saturday of the Apostles, the last day of the season. Both sets of readings printed in the calendar are shown: the four readings of the feast and the weekday readings. The calendar's headings for the feast: “God put the man whom He had formed, in Eden”; “Keep hold of instruction, for she is your life”; “The household of God, built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets”; “My Lord and my God”. For the Saturday: “Wife should not separate from the husband”; “God created them as man and woman”. Verify locally the times of the Holy Qurbana. Many also mark today as Syro-Malabar Church Day and as Indian Christian Day (verify locally). The Latin Church keeps the feast of Saint Thomas the Apostle today, and in India with special joy; tomorrow the Season of Kaitha begins.
2027-07-03.verse: Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!” Jesus said to him, “Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.”
theo: “Dukhrana” is a Syriac word that means remembrance. Each year on 3 July our Church remembers Mar Thoma, the Apostle Thomas, whom we call our father in faith. According to the East Syriac tradition, this is the day on which his relics were solemnly brought to Edessa, and so the day became his memorial; in the Syro-Malabar Church it is an important feast and a day of obligation. It is also the last day of the Season of the Apostles, and the season could not close with a better name. Thomas is the apostle whom the Gospel of John knows best after Peter and the beloved disciple. Three times he speaks. When Jesus decided to return to Judea, where his enemies were waiting, it was Thomas who said to the others, “Let us also go, that we may die with him.” At the Last Supper, when Jesus said “you know the way”, it was Thomas who said what the others were thinking: “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?” And on the second Sunday of Easter he spoke the greatest words in the Gospel. We have been unfair to Thomas by calling him only the doubter. He is the brave one, the honest one, and the one who confessed.

The Gospel is one of the most loved passages of John. Thomas was not with the others on Easter evening when Jesus came, and the ten told him, “We have seen the Lord.” He answered, “Unless I see the mark of the nails in his hands, and put my finger in the mark of the nails and my hand in his side, I will not believe.” Thomas asked for no more than the others had already received, since Jesus had “showed them his hands and his side” on the first evening. And Jesus did not refuse. “A week later his disciples were again in the house, and Thomas was with them.” The Lord came again, “Although the doors were shut”, and said, “Peace be with you.” Then he turned to Thomas by name and gave him what he had asked: “Put your finger here and see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it in my side. Do not doubt but believe.” The Gospel does not say that Thomas touched. It says that he answered, and what he answered is the climax of the whole book: “My Lord and my God!” The Gospel began with “the Word was God”; now a disciple says it to the face of the risen Jesus. The Catechism notes that even in the presence of the risen Lord some disciples doubted, and that the Lord's patient dealing with their doubt is part of the Church's faith (CCC 644). Then comes a blessing for us: “Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.” That is the Indian Church, and every church after the apostles: “Although you have not seen him, you love him; and even though you do not see him now, you believe in him and rejoice with an indescribable and glorious joy.”

The Epistle tells us what the apostles are to the Church: “So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone. In him the whole structure is joined together and grows into a holy temple in the Lord; in whom you also are built together spiritually into a dwelling place for God.” The Church is apostolic because she is founded on the apostles, and because the teaching they handed on is kept in her by their successors, the bishops (CCC 857). For us in India this is not abstract. Our community has always said that it received the faith directly from an apostle. According to tradition, Thomas came by sea to Muziris, near Kodungallur, in the year 52, preached to Jews and others on the Malabar coast, baptised, and founded communities at Kodungallur, Palayoor, Kokkamangalam, Kottakkavu, Niranam, Nilackal and Kollam, and then travelled further to the east coast, where he was martyred at Mylapore about the year 72; his tomb is venerated in the San Thome Basilica at Chennai. Historians weigh the sources with care, and the tradition has been held with unbroken love by the Thomas Christians for nearly two thousand years: in the ancient Acts of Thomas, in the memory of the Church of the East, in the songs and customs of our families. The Orthodox, Mar Thoma and Malankara Churches honour the same apostle, and today we rejoice with them in the one Lord whom Thomas confessed.

Why does the Church read Genesis on this day? The calendar chooses a passage about a garden in the east: “And the Lord God planted a garden in Eden, in the east; and there he put the man whom he had formed.” In the middle of the garden stands “the tree of life”; “A river flows out of Eden to water the garden”; and “The Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to till it and keep it.” The Bible ends where it begins: in the last book, “On either side of the river is the tree of life with its twelve kinds of fruit… and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations”, and the risen Lord promises, “To everyone who conquers, I will give permission to eat from the tree of life that is in the paradise of God.” Our East Syriac fathers, above all Saint Ephrem, loved to sing of this paradise, and of the Church as the garden that God plants again. On Easter morning Mary Magdalene thought the risen Lord was the gardener. Thomas was given a garden to till and keep: a garden in the east, watered by rivers, where the tree of the cross would stand and where the leaves of the tree would heal people. The rivers of the Malabar coast meet the sea near Kodungallur, and by tradition the preaching of the apostle there was the first stream of the river of the Gospel in our land.

The second reading is from the book of Proverbs, the voice of Wisdom speaking to a child: “Hear, my child, and accept my words, that the years of your life may be many. I have taught you the way of wisdom; I have led you in the paths of uprightness.” And: “Keep hold of instruction; do not let go; guard her, for she is your life.” The Thomas Christians have done exactly this. For centuries, without a ruling power to protect them and often without many books, they kept hold of the instruction handed down to them: the Qurbana, the Creed, the sign of the cross, the fasts, the family prayer, and the memory of Thomas, whom they called the Way of Thomas, Mar Thoma Margam. The sage's last verse is the promise for those who keep to the path: “But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, which shines brighter and brighter until full day.” Thomas once asked, “How can we know the way?” and Jesus answered, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.” We owe to the honest question of Thomas one of the greatest sayings of the Lord.

The weekday readings of the Seventh Saturday also have something to say on this feast. Paul, in the first letter to the Corinthians, speaks to the married and the unmarried about the practical shape of Christian faith in a household. “To the married I give this command, not I but the Lord, that the wife should not separate from her husband… and that the husband should not divorce his wife.” Where one partner is not yet a believer, he says that the believing partner should not cast the other aside: “For the unbelieving husband is made holy through his wife, and the unbelieving wife is made holy through her husband.” The Catechism uses this verse for the task of the Catholic spouse in a marriage with a person of another faith (CCC 1637). Paul's last word is a gentle one: “It is to peace that God has called you. Wife, for all you know, you might save your husband. Husband, for all you know, you might save your wife.” The Gospel takes us back to the beginning, to the same Genesis: “Have you not read that the one who made them at the beginning ‘made them male and female,’ and said, ‘For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh’? So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.” Jesus names the hardness of heart which made Moses permit divorce, and says, “from the beginning it was not so”; the Church holds the indissolubility of marriage as a gift of Christ and also accompanies with mercy those whose marriages have been wounded (CCC 1614–1615, 1640). Faith came to India through families, and it is handed on by families still. The garden of Eden was a home before it was a Church, and the Church has always been a household.

On this feast the Church prays that the faith of Thomas, tested and then confessed, be ours. Many Syro-Malabar people today go on pilgrimage to the churches that tradition links with the apostle, or sing the old songs of Mar Thoma. But the best Dukhrana is a daily one: to say at the elevation in the Qurbana, in our own heart, “My Lord and my God”, and then to carry the same Lord to those who have not yet seen. Thomas is the apostle of India and of the Church of the East; the Syro-Malabar Church today carries his mission to every state of India and to many countries of the world. May the Apostle who said “Let us also go” make us willing to go.
conn: “Thomas, who was called the Twin, said to his fellow disciples, ‘Let us also go, that we may die with him’” (John 11:16).

“Thomas said to him, ‘Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?’ Jesus said to him, ‘I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me’” (John 14:5–6).

“After he said this, he showed them his hands and his side. Then the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord. Jesus said to them again, ‘Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, so I send you’” (John 20:20–21).
“But these are written so that you may come to believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that through believing you may have life in his name” (John 20:31).
“And the wall of the city has twelve foundations, and on them are the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb” (Revelation 21:14).
“She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her; those who hold her fast are called happy” (Proverbs 3:18); “the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations” (Revelation 22:2).
To the ends of the world.
“Their voice has gone out to all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world” (Romans 10:18); “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation” (Mark 16:15).
outline: Dukhrana, remembrance: the apostle who said “Let us also go”, “How can we know the way?” and “My Lord and my God!”
Point 1 · My Lord and my God
Thomas asks for what the others had been given; Jesus comes again for him; the highest confession of the Gospel; the blessing on those who have not seen.
Point 2 · The foundation of the apostles
The Church is apostolic; the Thomas tradition in India, held “according to tradition” with love; Mylapore and the seven communities.
Point 3 · The garden in the east
The planted garden, the river and the tree of life; the Church as God's garden; the Gospel as a river in our land.
The path of the righteous like the light of dawn; the Way of Thomas kept for two thousand years; I am the way.
Point 5 · What God has joined together
Peace in the household; the family as the first church.
live: At the elevation of the Holy Qurbana this Sunday, say quietly in your heart, “My Lord and my God.” Say it also whenever you see a crucifix this week.
Choose one place or person you have avoided because it is hard to go there, a sick relative, a quarrel, an old friend, and go this week.
Tell your children or grandchildren the story of how the faith came to your family, and teach them the prayer of Thomas.
fathers: Thomas's unbelief helped our faith more than the faith of the disciples who believed at once. When he touched the wounds, our own hesitation was healed. The Lord allowed him to doubt so that the doubt might be cured by touch and that we, who come later, might be strengthened.
Thomas saw and touched a man, and confessed God, whom he neither saw nor touched. What he saw and touched removed every doubt, and his confession reaches beyond what his eyes and hands could reach.
magis: Even before the risen Lord, the disciples still doubted. Thomas himself met the test of doubt, and when Jesus showed him the wounds in his hands and side he said, “My Lord and my God!” The Church's faith in the Resurrection is built on these witnesses.

The Church is apostolic because she is founded on the apostles, in three ways: she was and remains built on their witness, she keeps and hands on their teaching, and she continues to be taught and guided by them through their successors, the bishops.
saints: Dukhrana of Saint Thomas the Apostle, an important feast and a day of obligation in the Syro-Malabar calendar; also the Seventh Saturday of the Apostles. The Latin Church keeps the feast of Saint Thomas the Apostle today, and in India with special joy. Indian Christian Day and Syro-Malabar Church Day are marked on this day (verify locally).

Sun 4 July: First Sunday of Kaitha, Feast of the Twelve Apostles. Mon 5 and Tue 6: the first Monday and Tuesday of Kaitha; Tue 6 also St Maria Goretti. Fri 9 July: First Friday of Kaitha, St James of Nisibis.
2027-07-03.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you came through closed doors and showed the wounds of your love to your disciple Thomas, and he answered, “My Lord and my God!” Give us the faith of Thomas: courage to go with you even to death, honesty to ask the way, and humility to adore. We thank you for the apostle who, according to tradition, brought the Gospel to our land, and for all the parents, teachers and ancestors who have handed it on. Keep us on the Way, make us strong in your peace, and send us as witnesses to those who have not yet seen. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Church does for us what the Lord did for Thomas: after the consecration the priest shows us the Body and the Blood, and we answer with our whole heart, “My Lord and my God.” The doors are shut, the Lord stands in our midst and says, “Peace be with you”, and he gives us his wounds as the food of life. Thomas touched, or was invited to touch, a body that had been wounded; at the altar we receive that same Body, now glorified. “Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.”

The altar is also the foundation stone of the household of God. Built on the foundation of the apostles, with Christ as cornerstone, the Church gathers round the altar, and the whole structure “grows into a holy temple in the Lord”. Here the faith that Thomas brought, the Qurbana in the East Syriac tradition, is celebrated as our fathers celebrated it, and here the family that God has joined together learns to be one.

quick: Dukhrana (remembrance) of Mar Thoma, the Apostle Thomas, our father in faith: an important feast and a day of obligation; the last day of the Season of the Apostles.
John: a week after Easter Jesus comes again for Thomas, shows his wounds, and Thomas confesses, “My Lord and my God!”; blessed are those who have not seen and believe.

Ephesians: the Church is built on the foundation of the apostles, with Christ as the cornerstone; Genesis and Proverbs: the garden in the east, the tree of life, and the path of the righteous like the light of dawn.
The Seventh Saturday: Paul calls married people to peace and fidelity; Jesus recalls God's plan for marriage from the beginning.
2027-07-03.action: At the elevation in the Qurbana, say in your heart, “My Lord and my God,” and tell one young person how the faith came to your family.
2027-07-03.question: If I could ask the risen Lord for one sign, what would it be, and am I ready to say “My Lord and my God” even without it?
catechism: Thomas and the doubt of the disciples.
Marriage from the beginning; Jesus and Moses' permission.
The believing spouse in a marriage with a non-believer.
The marriage bond and the Church's care.
kidsaint: Thomas was one of Jesus' twelve friends. He was brave: when Jesus was going to a dangerous place, Thomas said, ‘Let us also go!’ He asked honest questions, too. When Jesus rose from the dead, Thomas was not there, and he said, ‘I will believe when I see.’ Jesus came back for him, and Thomas said, ‘My Lord and my God!’ After that Thomas went far away. According to tradition he came by boat to Kerala, told people about Jesus, baptised them and started churches, and he died at Mylapore near Chennai. Lesson: ask your questions, be brave, and tell others about Jesus, as Thomas did!
2027-07-03.special: Dukhrana of St Thomas the Apostle: an important feast and a day of obligation; the last day of the Season of the Apostles. Kaitha begins tomorrow.
term: A Syriac word meaning remembrance or memorial. In the East Syriac tradition, 3 July is the Dukhrana of St Thomas, the day on which his relics are remembered as brought to Edessa. In the Syro-Malabar Church it is the great feast of our father in faith. Malayalam: ദുക്റാന.

family.explain: Thomas was one of Jesus' friends. After Jesus rose from the dead, Thomas was not in the room when Jesus came, and the others told him, ‘We have seen the Lord!’ Thomas said, ‘I will believe only when I see.’ Eight days later Jesus came again and said to Thomas, ‘Peace be with you. Look at my hands.’ Thomas said, ‘My Lord and my God!’ And Jesus said that people who believe without seeing are blessed: that means us! Our Church says that Thomas came to Kerala by boat and told our people about Jesus, so Thomas is our father in faith.
family.intention: We thank God for the faith of our grandparents and for every priest, sister and teacher who handed it on, and we pray for all Christians of India.
family.ask: Ask: “Who first told us about Jesus in our family, and how can we thank them?”

illus: In a parish near Palayoor (a story told to illustrate the reading) a boy of ten once asked his grandmother after the Dukhrana Qurbana, ‘Ammachi, did Mar Thoma really come here? How do you know?’ The old woman smiled. ‘I was not there, mon, and neither was my mother. But my mother's mother told my mother, and my mother told me, and I have told you. In our family every grandmother has said, Mar Thoma brought us the faith. That is how we know: someone told someone, and each one loved enough to pass it on.’ The boy thought for a while and said, ‘So it is like Thomas and the Lord. He did not see Mar Thoma, but he believes.’ The grandmother laughed and touched his head. ‘Blessed are those who have not seen, my child, and yet have believed.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you came through closed doors and said “Peace” to your disciples and to Thomas. Gather us in your name and give us the faith of Thomas. Amen.
share: Let us also go, that we may die with him (John 11:16). Where is Jesus calling me to go, even though it is hard?
How can we know the way? (John 14:5). What question about my faith do I carry, and have I brought it to the Lord?
Put your finger here and see my hands (John 20:27). How have I seen the Lord's wounds in the poor and the suffering?
My Lord and my God! (John 20:28). Can I say this today from my heart, and what would change if I meant it?
interc: For the Church in India, founded on the faith of Saint Thomas, that she may remain faithful and be a sign of Christ in every land.
For the Syro-Malabar Church and her missions in India and across the world.
For all Christians who share the heritage of Saint Thomas, the Orthodox, Mar Thoma and Malankara Churches, that we may grow in unity and peace.
For those who doubt and for those who are searching for the truth, that they may find Christ.
For families, that they may be places where faith is handed on and where the peace of Christ is lived.
pm.close: Father, you gave the Church of India the apostle Thomas as father in faith. Through his prayers keep us on the Way, make us glad witnesses of your Son, and bring us to the joy of those who believe without seeing. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today is the Dukhrana of Mar Thoma, Saint Thomas the Apostle, our father in faith. The word Dukhrana means remembrance. Today the Church remembers him, and we remember that the faith of our families and our parish comes, according to our oldest tradition, from an apostle of Jesus.

Thomas is often called the doubter, but he was much more. When Jesus went toward danger, Thomas said to the others, “Let us also go, that we may die with him” (John 11:16). When he did not understand, he asked: “How can we know the way?” (John 14:5). He was brave, and he was honest.

On Easter evening Thomas was not with the others. They told him, “We have seen the Lord.” He said that he could not believe unless he saw the wounds. A week later Jesus came again, through closed doors, and said, “Peace be with you.” Then Jesus turned to Thomas: “Put your finger here and see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it in my side. Do not doubt but believe” (John 20:27). Thomas did not need to touch. He said, “My Lord and my God!” This is the highest confession in the whole Gospel.

And Jesus said: “Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe” (John 20:29). That is us. We have not seen Jesus with our eyes. But we have seen the faith of our parents, and we have received the Body of the Lord in the Qurbana. Saint Paul says that we are built on the foundation of the apostles, with Christ as the cornerstone (Ephesians 2:20). Thomas is one of those foundation stones for our Church in India.

The calendar also gives us the Garden of Eden and the Book of Proverbs. In Eden God puts the man in a garden “to till it and keep it” (Genesis 2:15). Thomas was given a garden in the east to till and keep. And Proverbs says, “Keep hold of instruction; do not let go; guard her, for she is your life” (Proverbs 4:13). Our ancestors kept hold of the faith for nearly two thousand years. What are we keeping hold of, and what are we handing on?

Today in the Saturday readings, Jesus and Saint Paul speak about marriage and peace in the home. The faith came to India in families and lives in families. Let us pray for our homes: “It is to peace that God has called you” (1 Corinthians 7:15). And let us say this week, at the elevation of the Holy Qurbana, the prayer of Thomas: “My Lord and my God.” Amen.
kids: Children, today is the feast of Saint Thomas, who came to our India with the good news of Jesus. Thomas was brave and he asked honest questions. When Jesus came back after Easter, Thomas said the most beautiful words: ‘My Lord and my God!’
You can say those words, too! When you see the priest lift the Body of Jesus at the Holy Qurbana, say in your heart: ‘My Lord and my God!’ And thank God for the people who taught you to pray.

intro: On the Dukhrana of Saint Thomas the Apostle: the apostle who said “Let us also go”, the Lord who comes again for the one who is missing, the foundation of the apostles, the garden in the east and the path like the light of dawn.

concl: Thomas asked, went and confessed: “My Lord and my God!” Through him, according to tradition, the Gospel reached our land, and the Church is built on the foundation of the apostles.
We keep hold of the instruction we received, we guard the garden, and we hand on the faith to those who have not seen.
2027-07-03.resolve: This week, say Thomas's prayer at the elevation, thank one person who handed on the faith to you, and pray with your family for peace in the home.
